panels.description: Live queue depth per entity. RSS uses scrape_queue_size (set once at scraper startup; reflects the seed working set). Channel uses channel_queue_tier_size summed across tiers. Video uses video_state_size{state="queued"} (Redis-backed; max-by-state collapses the duplicate per-host publishers).
panels.title: Total queue depth

Video: files_pending_upload{entity="video"} from yt_video_upload.py (returns no data until the gauge is wired in the video upload tool).
panels.title: Files waiting for upload
Uploads per second by entity × mode

panels.description: Per-proxy_file success and failure rate (5m) of RSS feed fetches by the RSS scraper. Use this to spot networks where the RSS path is degrading. Compare with the YouTube scraper's circuit-breaker panel to see whether degradation tripped the limiter.
panels.title: RSS fetch Failure rate

panels.description: Per-proxy_file success and failure rate (5m) of InnerTube channel.info calls made by the RSS scraper. Use to spot networks where InnerTube channel resolution is degrading.
panels.title: InnerTube Channel fail rate by proxy_file

panels.description: Per-proxy_file failure rate (5m) of InnerTube video.info calls made by the RSS scraper. Use to spot networks where InnerTube video resolution is degrading.
panels.title: InnerTube Video call fail ratio by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the TCP handshake to the proxy on RSS fetches. Histograms only record fresh connection establishment — keep-alive reuse skips the trace event, so _count reflects new tunnels, not total fetches.
panels.title: RSS TCP connect duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the HTTP CONNECT exchange (proxy dialing YouTube on our behalf) on RSS fetches. The gap between connect_tcp.complete and start_tls.started — i.e. the proxy backend's dial-out queue.
panels.title: RSS HTTP CONNECT tunnel duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the TLS handshake to YouTube via the proxy tunnel on RSS fetches. Slowness here — with fast TCP and HTTP CONNECT — indicates YouTube is throttling TLS from the proxy's egress IP rather than provider-side queueing.
panels.title: RSS TLS handshake duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the TCP handshake to the proxy on YouTube HTML fetches (channel about-page, home, search, session warm-up). Sourced from curl's CURLINFO_CONNECT_TIME minus CURLINFO_NAMELOOKUP_TIME. Histograms only record fresh connection establishment — keep-alive reuse skips because curl reports 0 for the connect-related fields on reuse.
panels.title: HTML TCP connect duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the TLS handshake (plus HTTP CONNECT tunnel exchange for proxied requests) on YouTube HTML fetches. Sourced from curl's CURLINFO_APPCONNECT_TIME minus CURLINFO_CONNECT_TIME. Note: curl reports app-connect cumulatively, so the HTTP CONNECT exchange cannot be split out separately as it is on RSS — both are bundled here. Slowness with fast TCP indicates YouTube is throttling TLS from the proxy's egress IP or the provider's CONNECT-tunnel queue is backed up.
panels.title: HTML TLS handshake (+CONNECT) duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the TCP handshake to the proxy on InnerTube calls (channel.browse / video.player). Sourced from httpcore trace events on the third-party innertube library's httpx.Client session. Histograms only record fresh connection establishment — keep-alive reuse skips the trace event.
panels.title: InnerTube TCP connect duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the HTTP CONNECT exchange (proxy dialing YouTube on our behalf) on InnerTube calls. Gap between connect_tcp.complete and start_tls.started — the proxy backend's dial-out queue.
panels.title: InnerTube HTTP CONNECT tunnel duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: p50 / p95 of the TLS handshake to YouTube via the proxy tunnel on InnerTube calls. Slowness with fast TCP + fast CONNECT indicates YouTube is throttling TLS from the proxy's egress IP.
panels.title: InnerTube TLS handshake duration (p50/p95) by proxy_file

panels.description: Fraction of requests that reused an existing pooled TCP connection (didn't need a new TCP+CONNECT+TLS handshake). High = the TLS handshake cost amortises across many requests; low = every fetch pays the full handshake cost, and the TLS p95 numbers turn into your wall-clock floor. Broken out by call_type so you can see whether RSS/InnerTube/HTML pools are reusing equally well.
panels.title: Keep-alive reuse rate by call_type

panels.description: Average requests per fresh TCP connection. A value of 1 means every request opens a fresh connection (worst case — full handshake cost per fetch). 10 means each connection serves 10 requests on average before the pool retires it. Higher is better; large differences across proxy_files indicate that some providers terminate the keep-alive earlier than others.

targets.expr: sum by (call_type, proxy_file) (rate(proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) / clamp_max(sum by (call_type, proxy_file) (rate(proxy_requests_total{reused="false",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[5m])), 100)

panels.title: Requests per fresh connection by call_type x proxy_file

panels.description: Number of yt-dlp extract_info calls currently in the thread pool. Pins near executor ceiling (≈12 per process) when GIL / executor is the bottleneck.
panels.title: yt-dlp extract_info active (thread-pool occupancy)

panels.description: Number of entries in the video scraper's priority directory (YOUTUBE_VIDEO_PRIORITY_DIRECTORY). Sampled on every workload-prep cycle. Falling trend = workers draining the backlog; rising trend = priority-write producers outpacing the scraper.
panels.title: Priority directory size (video scraper)

panels.description: Resolve-phase outcomes per attempt. Outcomes: promoted (success), not_found, inconsistent_identity, backoff (transient retry), unresolved (gave up).

panels.description: Scrape-phase outcomes per attempt. Outcomes: scraped (success), not_found, terminated, soft_unavailable (transient), unresolved (no handle in creator_map).

panels.description: Number of videos currently in each workflow state. Gauge is published by one elected worker per host, so max-by-state collapses the duplicate series.

panels.description: Per-attempt outcomes in the video scrape queue. Outcomes: scraped (success or already-uploaded dedup), retried (transient failure, bump_attempts), unavailable (private / age-gated / removed), failed (other or transient retries exhausted).
